verdict_note: From reading only: no build and no tests were run. Line anchors are crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/tests/diag_sink.rs at 3ea45cdd unless a file is named. The core fix holds. assert_died_without_a_record (:714-728) keeps every assertion in the brief's fix contract: nonzero exit, no studio-panic-* file, segment_start/run_start/op in order, last line op, and survey (0, 1, 1). The Windows abort test also asserts exit code 3 (:745-748), and every child that dies without a record must report SEM_NOGPFAULTERRORBOX (:716-719). The fix removes the WER cause by mechanism. In the UCRT 10.0.26100 source, abort() with _CALL_REPORTFAULT cleared and no SIGABRT handler skips __fastfail and calls _exit(3) (ucrt/startup/abort.cpp), and nothing in harness-core installs a SIGABRT handler. The guard cannot run forever: steps count only in order over three fixed marks, so a run is bounded at 4 deadlines (240 s), as :600-602 states. The FFI declarations are correctly typed and are called only on child paths. The cfg gates for non-Windows targets are correct by reading. No product defect is masked: src/diag_sink.rs writes each line straight to an unbuffered File and has no Drop, no flush on exit and no signal handler. There are three low findings. F1: on Windows the abort test now proves an ExitProcess death, not the fast fail that every Rust abort takes. Nothing is masked today; record this or switch to TerminateProcess. F2: the hang test does not prove the kill, because a no-op kill still passes. F3: the v4_06 reason 'not applicable' for harden_worker_process does not hold for Rust's own fast fail in workers. F2 is the fix-first item: a few lines in the owned test file.

findings.what: Before this lane, the Windows abort child died through std::process::abort, a fast fail after which no user-mode code runs. Every Rust abort path on Windows dies this way: std::process::abort, rtabort!, a double panic, a panic in a no-unwind frame and panic=abort. It is also the class the original lane names (R56's composer abort). The child now dies through the C runtime abort. With the report fault off, that calls _exit(3), and _exit ends a desktop process with ExitProcess: the other threads end, then every loaded DLL runs its DLL_PROCESS_DETACH entry. On Windows the abort test therefore proves the sink against a softer death than the one it stands for. Today no outcome changes. The sink writes each line with one write_all on an unbuffered File (put :370-374), has no Drop, flush-on-exit or atexit path, and its only thread local is IN_HOOK, a Cell<bool>. The overflow test (:730-739) still covers a Windows death with no cleanup (unhandled STATUS_STACK_OVERFLOW, exit 0xC00000FD). The gap is in the future. A sink change that buffers lines and flushes them from a path that runs at process exit would pass the Windows abort test while a real Rust abort loses those lines. Linux and macOS keep std::process::abort, but the lanes and rounds run on Windows.
findings.scenario: Mutation, by reading: a later change gives the sink a buffered writer that is flushed by a destructor reached at DLL detach or FLS cleanup, for example a sink held in a thread local with a Drop. Under fast fail the buffered op line is lost. Under _exit(3), which calls ExitProcess, that path can flush it, and the Windows abort test stays green. Whether Rust's FLS-based TLS destructors run on the ExitProcess path is NOT_INSPECTED. DLL_PROCESS_DETACH entries do run.
findings.fix: Either (a) or (b), the same size. (a) End the Windows abort child with TerminateProcess(GetCurrentProcess(), 3): one kernel32 call with a pseudo-handle and no pointer. It brings no Windows Error Reporting, no DLL detach and no TLS or FLS callback, and the exit code stays 3, so the Windows proof keeps fast fail's no-cleanup property. (b) Keep the C runtime abort (the harden_worker_process precedent the lead accepted) and record the reading in the comment at :493-495 and in the lane file's decision_for_lead: the Windows abort test proves an ExitProcess death, and the overflow test carries the no-cleanup death.
findings.test: (a): no new test. The abort test's exit code 3 assertion still pins the path. (b): none.

findings.what: This lane measured that the error mode does not keep a fast fail out of Windows Error Reporting. _CALL_REPORTFAULT changes only the C runtime's abort(), and Rust's own aborts do not go through it. std::process::abort, rtabort!, a double panic, a panic that reaches a no-unwind frame (an extern "C" boundary) and the default allocation-error handler all end in abort_internal, which is int 0x29. A worker process that dies one of these ways is still held by WerFault for seconds. By job.rs:51-53's own account, it then surfaces as a deadline kill instead of a crash. So harden_worker_process covers native (C) aborts and unhandled exceptions, not Rust's fast fail. 'Not applicable' is right for this lane's scope, but wrong as a reason.
findings.scenario: By reading: a QuickJS or EPS worker panics while panicking, or panics inside a callback that the C side calls through a no-unwind boundary. Rust aborts by fast fail, and `WerFault.exe -u -p <worker>` holds the process. The supervisor's deadline fires first, and the job is classified as a deadline, not a crash. UNVERIFIED: whether any such path is reachable in the shipped workers.

answers.sink_semantics: Kept. assert_died_without_a_record (:714-728) still asserts that the code is not 0, that there is no studio-panic-* file, and that segment_start, run_start and op come in order with the op's fields. It also asserts that the last line is op (no run_end) and the survey (panic_files 0, unterminated_runs 1, runs_surveyed 1). All three death tests (overflow, abort, slow abort) use it. Two assertions are added. On Windows the reported error mode must have SEM_NOGPFAULTERRORBOX (:716-719). The Windows abort exit code must be 3 (:745-748), which pins the C runtime abort path: a regression to fast fail exits 0xC0000409 and fails. The sink calls before the abort are unchanged (:521-523). The per-step sleep comes after record_op, so the lines are on disk before any delay (the abort test uses step 0). The softer Windows death is F1.
answers.guard_ceiling: No run is unbounded. steps_reached (:559-567) counts only in-order matches of the three CHILD_STEPS over all stderr so far. The count therefore only grows and stops at 3, and repeated or out-of-order marks never reset the clock. life resets only when the count grows (:640-643). A run is at most four deadlines plus poll slack, which is 240 s at CHILD_DEADLINE 60 s, as documented at :602. Beyond that implicit bound there is no explicit absolute ceiling. A real hang is still killed one deadline after its last step; a hang before entered is killed at 60 s, as before. The worst case, with each step just under 60 s, is 4x the old 60 s cap and needs a child that keeps progressing.
answers.unsafe_ffi: Correct by reading. GetErrorMode() -> UINT and SetErrorMode(UINT) -> UINT are declared in kernel32 with extern "system". abort() -> ! and _set_abort_behavior(unsigned, unsigned) -> unsigned are declared with extern "C" (cdecl), matching ucrt stdlib.h and the hsk-studio-worker declaration (job.rs:44-47). No pointer crosses the boundary, and `safe fn` is sound for all four: they write process-wide flags, and abort is as safe as std::process::abort. The flags (SEM_NOGPFAULTERRORBOX 0x2, _WRITE_ABORT_MSG 0x1, _CALL_REPORTFAULT 0x2) match job.rs:38-42. _set_abort_behavior(0, 0x3) clears both bits: abort.cpp computes old & ~mask | flags & mask. The calls are confined to the child. keep_the_crash_reporter_out (:517) and mark run only after the CHILD_ENV check in child_entry (:516), and abort() runs only in the abort arm (:531). The parent only parses the mode the child reports. mod win exists only under cfg(windows). The safe declarations could be called from any code in the test crate, but no parent path calls them. The UCRT symbols link through the CRT that std already links, as the worker crate also relies on. The toolchain targets are msvc only (rust-toolchain.toml 1.97.1; installed std for x86_64 and aarch64 msvc, wasm32 and linux-musl), so windows-gnu linkage was not considered. On aarch64-msvc, the cleared _CALL_REPORTFAULT also skips the __fastfail branch.
answers.masks_product_defect: No. The measured hold is in Windows Error Reporting after the abort call. The child's own work took 30-34 ms. From ending to exit took 3.2-13.1 s alone before the fix and takes 14-18 ms after it. In src/diag_sink.rs, every line is one write_all on an unbuffered std::fs::File opened for append (open_file :142-146, put :370-374), so each line reaches the OS before record returns. A grep over harness-core src finds no impl Drop, no BufWriter or LineWriter, and no signal or atexit handler. PROCESS_SINK is a static OnceLock and is never dropped, and the only thread local is IN_HOOK (Cell<bool>). Neither death path changes what is on disk. Only the coverage shifts (F1).
answers.non_windows: Unchanged and compiling, by reading. Not compiled; the lane also lists this as not_proven. mod win is #[cfg(windows)]. error_mode, keep_the_crash_reporter_out and abort each have a cfg(not(windows)) body or an empty one (None, nothing, std::process::abort()). The tail-position #[cfg] block is the pattern error_mode already used at b4d5854e. No win:: name is used outside cfg(windows). The error-mode check uses the literal 0x0002 inside if cfg!(windows) (:716-719), so it still type-checks on other targets. The CommandExt creation flag stays cfg(windows) (:612-617). Off Windows, the abort child still calls std::process::abort (SIGABRT), and the extra error-mode and exit-3 assertions are skipped. The guard change applies on every platform. The phase marks go to stderr only.
answers.determinism: The target test, an_abort_leaves_the_lines_written_and_no_end_of_run, is deterministic by mechanism. Windows Error Reporting no longer holds the child: the C runtime abort runs with the report fault off, ending to exit measured 14-18 ms, and the lane's WER watcher saw no WerFault process in two runs. Each step also has its own 60 s guard. The two new tests use a 5 s guard. Spawn to entered measured 30 ms alone, and the earlier bundled run at 81de18b9 ended its clean, panic and overflow children in 0.28-0.79 s under D: load, so the margin is about 6x. In the slow-abort test each quiet window is 3 s plus the sink's work against 5 s, a 2 s margin. These tests tolerate load but do not ignore it: a stall of more than 5 s in child start-up would fail them. A deadline of 10 s with a step of 6 s would add margin at the cost of 6 s more test time. That is not a finding. The bundled run has not been done yet (lane file).
answers.red_test_integrity: The red test body is unchanged between b4d5854e and 3ea45cdd, so it was not rewritten to pass (common ruling 11). The red result recorded at b4d5854e (killed at +5000 ms, lines_written at +3030 ms) matches the from-spawn guard at that commit. The fix commit changes only the guard and the death path.
